extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers of Cochrane Hepato-Biliary Group (CHBG) protocols and reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing peer review of Cochrane Hepato-Biliary Group protocols and reviews, including required reviewer composition, ethical expectations, procedural steps, and quality/format expectations. Refers reviewers to the appropriate Cochrane Handbooks for detailed methodological standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify review type and follow appropriate Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four types of Cochrane reviews: Intervention reviews, Diagnostic test accuracy reviews, Overview of reviews, and Methodology reviews. Peer reviewers of Intervention protocols/reviews are referred to the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and reviewers of Diagnostic Test Accuracy protocols/reviews are referred to the Cochrane Handbook for Diagnostic Test Accuracy Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which of the four review types the manuscript is and apply the corresponding Cochrane Handbook guidance for preparation and methodological standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer composition (who should review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to publication, a protocol or a review is reviewed by at least one or more persons from each of the following groups: Cochrane review authors working in the area of interest, consumers or representatives of consumers acting as consumer peer reviewers, health-care professionals who are not Cochrane review authors, statisticians or methods experts, developing countries representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the peer reviewer pool includes these perspectives so that methodological, clinical, consumer, statistical, and global viewpoints are represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: No direct financial or personal conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should not have direct financial or personal conflicts of interest concerning the topic addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All peer reviewers will be asked to declare any potential conflict of interest. If conflicts exist, recuse yourself or declare them per CHBG procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided checklist for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are sent a copy of the protocol and a checklist for comments to be returned to the CHBG Managing Editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base your review on the supplied checklist to ensure consistency and coverage of expected items; return the completed checklist with your comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide courteous and constructive comments identifying weaknesses and ways to improve
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask peer reviewers to submit courteous and constructive comments on the protocol that identify its weaknesses or fatal flaws, as well as ways of improving it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid demeaning statements; focus on constructive critique that pinpoints weaknesses or fatal flaws and offers concrete suggestions for improvement. All feedback forms and other comments will be forwarded to the review authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of review comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are usually requested to return these comments within a specified in the letter time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments within the requested timeframe to avoid delaying editorial processing; contact the Managing Editor if you cannot meet the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review / transparency of reviewer identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer reviewers’ process is ‘open’, i.e., no attempt will be made to hide the identity of the peer reviewers from anyone involved in the process as well as the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that your identity and feedback will be shared with authors and potentially publicly; therefore ensure professionalism and civility in all comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to COPE peer review ethical guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer reviewers are requested to adhere to the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) peer review ethical guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow COPE guidance on confidentiality, conflicts of interest, professional behaviour, and other ethical obligations during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that authors respond and editorial decision on comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors are requested to respond to the raised comments. The Contact Editor or the Co-ordinating Editor will have the final decision as to which of the peer reviewer’s comments need to be addressed in the event of disagreement between a peer reviewer and a team of authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that peer review is part of an iterative process: your comments will be forwarded to authors, authors should respond, and the Contact/Co-ordinating Editor will arbitrate disagreements and make final publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider use of ARCADIA to assess quality of peer-review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: ARCADIA: a tool for assessing the quality of peer-review reports in biomedical research (referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use or consult ARCADIA as a resource for what constitutes a high-quality peer-review report (e.g., coverage, clarity, usefulness of recommendations), when preparing or evaluating peer-review feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHBG in-house peer review and quality assurance prior to central editorial submission
rubrics_metrics.description: CHBG is still conducting in-house peer review and quality assurance before a manuscript is submitted to the Cochrane Central Editorial Service for final peer review and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect CHBG to perform an internal editorial check and quality assurance step; tailor reviews to meet both CHBG internal standards and the broader Cochrane editorial requirements.
